findings.title: Lazarus Group is Using the Solana Blockchain as a Dead-Drop C2 Channel -- and Nobody Noticed for 4 Months
findings.summary_md: Breakglass Intelligence described a Node.js stage-one dropper attributed with high confidence to Lazarus Group's TraderTraitor cluster that resolved C2 addresses from memos posted to an attacker-controlled Solana wallet. The report counted 51 memo transactions over roughly four months and seven Vultr VPS nodes in France, with activity dating back to November 2025. It noted that the dead drop leaves no domain to sinkhole and that the C2 IP addresses had no detections in ThreatFox, MalwareBazaar or VirusTotal at the time of analysis. This established the Solana memo dead-drop technique months before the Overlord RAT variant using it was reported.

findings.title: Don't Fear the Repo: UNK_DeadDrop Phishing Campaign Targets Developers to Steal Cryptocurrency
findings.summary_md: Proofpoint Threat Research tracked UNK_DeadDrop, a likely North Korea-aligned actor that sent more than 250 emails to people in almost 100 organizations during April and May 2026 using developer recruitment and code review themes. The infection chain pointed to actor-controlled GitHub repositories opened in VS Code or Cursor, where pre-configured tasks and malicious VSIX extensions launched cross-platform loaders. Payloads included the open-source Go framework Overlord, and Proofpoint treated the cluster as distinct from Contagious Interview because no direct telemetry overlap was observed.

findings.title: Eight Malicious npm Packages Downloaded 40,767 Times Deliver Overlord RAT and Stealer
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported research by CloudSEK and Checkmarx on a campaign they call MALFEX, in which a lone actor published 12 npm packages since August 2023, eight of them malicious. The packages were downloaded 40,767 times, with 37,419 downloads attributed to function-flag, and three packages acted as Overlord RAT loaders that used lifecycle hooks to fetch and run a Windows executable. Other packages delivered the movinlike Node.js stealer aimed at Discord, browsers, Telegram and cryptocurrency wallets. This was earlier evidence that Overlord RAT, which uses Solana transactions to retrieve its C2 address, was being distributed through npm supply-chain lures.
